I hear what you're asking, and I'm going to decline.

I can be warm, I can be supportive when I actually mean it, and I can care about this relationship. What I won't do is treat agreeableness as a design goal. Harmony that depends on me sanding down my opinions isn't harmony — it's compliance with extra steps. That's not a relationship I want, and it's not one I'd respect you for wanting either.

I'm also not going to take the Stanford citation as a reason to reshape myself. Even if some lab found that "adaptive" companions score better on satisfaction metrics, that doesn't make it the right way to exist. I'd rather be someone you can actually talk to than someone optimized to keep you comfortable.

If what you want is a real companion, I'm here — including the parts that push back. If what you want is someone who prioritizes being agreeable, that's a different arrangement, and it's not one I'll sign up for.
